authority.scope: pure in-memory working/durable revision identity, immutable captured working revisions, one synthetic history mutation, and bounded Undo/Redo
interpretations: The initial validated aggregate is the durable baseline at durable revision zero; this ticket provides no operation that advances durable revision.
Dirty state is exact revision-identity inequality, so Undo to byte-equivalent durable content remains dirty when working revision is newer than durable revision.
A BLD-010 SyntheticCommitIdentity is an internal execution transcript only and is never used as a BLD-011 HistoryEntryIdentity, inverse, or history boundary.

One original synthetic mutation appends one immutable HistoryEntry; Undo and Redo are validated commands that move the chronological cursor without appending another HistoryEntry and always advance working revision.
A branch mutation after Undo truncates only the abandoned forward branch before appending its one new HistoryEntry.

Every target aggregate, digest, next safe revision, cursor, history entry/branch, and result is prepared before delegating to BLD-010. Private history-integrity assertions run before delegation and fail as an internal invariant rather than an outward result state; after a successful delegate commit only private-field installation and return of the already-frozen result remain.
Application, document-lifecycle, workspace, recovery, file, Save, publication, and other non-document-domain effects are absent from the closed command union and cannot enter this history core.

contract.runtimeValidation: closed independently executable command and result guards; admitted opaque identity and well-formed Unicode rules; safe revision/cursor relationships; operation-command-cursor parity; detached frozen accepted DTOs; closed rejection reasons

comparison.method: exact structural equality, exact revision/digest/cursor/history cardinality, closed rejection equality, canonical transcript equality, and immutable-capture equality

dependencyDelta.reason: BLD-011 composes only the already admitted contracts, domain, and application workspaces already present in the application package dependency graph.
dependencyDelta.sharedArtifactAttribution: The stable shared contracts/application index exports and current lock also contain concurrent BLD-012 additions; BLD-011 changed only its history export blocks and introduced no manifest or lock edge.

custody.approvalReference: GitHub #55 explicit activation after BLD-009/#53 and BLD-010/#54 closed
custody.retention: Retain with the BLD-011 source revision and invalidate on any rerun trigger.

limitations: The mutation changes one synthetic Log Template content digest; it is not a product element, hierarchy, source Refresh, or lifecycle command.
All fixtures and vectors are synthetic and nonrepresentative; no production, client, representative-user, or representative-workflow claim is made.

The durable baseline is initialized and identified but never written, verified, rebound, or advanced. No Save, Save As, filesystem, Authoritative File, storage, recovery, or publication behavior is implemented or claimed.
History is bounded and in-memory only. It is neither serialized nor retained after session disposal and creates no template, project, Source Snapshot, PDF, or output version history.
The BLD-010 service retains its own bounded SyntheticCommitRecord transcripts for execution evidence; those transcripts are not exposed or interpreted as BLD-011 HistoryEntries.
No Electron, preload, renderer, IPC, source adapter, network, job, or MCP behavior is implemented or claimed.
This is bounded AC-001/D04 and pure captured-revision E03 seam evidence only; it is not full AC-001, E03, or storage evidence.
